claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Thermodynamic factors govern the phase stability of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 during cooling and thermal exposure.
Kinetic factors govern the phase stability of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 during cooling and thermal exposure.
CALPHAD combined with in situ X-ray diffraction and TEM can accurately predict the phase stability.
Controlled cooling and thermal exposure lead to the formation of precipitates and/or secondary phases.
The precipitates and/or secondary phases form through nucleation and growth.
Thermodynamic factors influence the nucleation and growth of precipitates and/or secondary phases.
Kinetic factors influence the nucleation and growth of precipitates and/or secondary phases.
Cooling rates of 0.1-10 K/s and thermal exposures at 500-1000°C for 1-100 hours define the proposed test conditions.
The baseline volume fraction of precipitates and/or secondary phases is 10%.
The specified cooling and thermal exposure will produce a 20-50% increase in precipitate and/or secondary-phase volume fraction relative to the 10% baseline.
In situ X-ray diffraction and TEM can measure the predicted precipitate and/or secondary-phase volume fraction.
At cooling rates above 10 K/s, kinetic factors dominate and thermodynamic equilibrium is not reached.
At thermal exposure temperatures above 1000°C, kinetic factors dominate and thermodynamic equilibrium is not reached.
A volume fraction below 15% or above 60% after exposure at 800°C for 10 hours is specified as a falsification result.

contradictions.description: A 20-50% relative increase from a 10% baseline corresponds to an absolute volume fraction of 12-15%, but the falsification rule rejects values below 15%. Thus nearly the entire stated predicted range would falsify the hypothesis. If '20-50% increase' instead means percentage points, the predicted absolute range would be 30-60%, which is not stated clearly.
